REPAIR-BEFORE-MERGE.

The theorem is faithful to the original open question: it preserves boundary and label-constant menus, adds no substantive assumptions, promises only weak approximation, and does not claim rational exact optimizers. The zero-face construction is also sound in principle: the multilinear Bernoulli extension is division-free and defines a total estimator; exact zero likelihood can be detected rationally, with arbitrary clipped decisions assigned there.

The primal and dual certificate logic is basically correct. In particular, G(π)=min_n b_n(π) is concave because it is an infimum of linear loss functions, direct rational evaluation gives G(π)≤R⋆, and any repaired feasible primal point gives an upper bound. The advertised ε-gap follows once the upper and lower errors are explicitly budgeted.

The present proof is nevertheless not a complete Turing-model proof:

- [GLS Theorem 4.3.13](https://www.zib.de/userpage/groetschel/pubnew/paper/groetschellovaszschrijver1988.pdf) requires a centered full-dimensional body with an explicit rational center and inner/outer radii, plus an approximate-value oracle for a convex function on every rational ambient-space query. The proof supplies only informal assertions that suitable balls and “nested versions” exist.
- The supplied primal oracle evaluates the perspective only for d_n≥η; the perspective is not a real-valued convex function on all ambient space. Likewise, the formula h²/a only supplies the stated dual oracle on the simplex. Thus the cited generic lemma cannot yet be invoked with the oracle model actually constructed.
- “Replace η by a constant multiple,” projection/clipping error, erosion loss, and “halve tolerances if necessary” do not give the explicit polynomially encoded radii and tolerance ledger required for the claimed bit bound.
- The decoder argument should explicitly output a polynomial-size rational arithmetic circuit/recursion and state its finite-input evaluation model; “arbitrary real v” cannot itself be exact Turing input.

The narrowest faithful repair keeps the theorem statement but repairs the reduction. Give explicit nested polytopes, centers, radii, and error allocations. Supply global exact rational convex oracles, for example extending each primal perspective on the feasible region by

    max_{u∈[-L,L]} [(2u−2θ)t + (θ²−u²)d],

which is globally convex, rationally evaluable, and agrees with (t−dθ)²/d when d>0 and |t|≤Ld. Extend the dual globally using its bounded-decision representation as an infimum of linear functions of π, evaluating each one-dimensional quadratic by a rational clipped stationary point or endpoint. Then apply the exact GLS weak-output specification, repair feasibility with quantified distance bounds, directly evaluate both certificates, and describe the decoder as a polynomial-size division-free arithmetic circuit. Until those items are supplied, merging would overstate a plausible proof sketch as the requested complete bit-complexity theorem.
why: The proposed theorem is faithful and the primal/dual strategy is plausible, but the cited weak-optimization reduction lacks the global oracle model, explicit full-dimensional geometry and radii, quantified tolerance accounting, and finite-input decoder circuit needed to establish the claimed Turing bit complexity. Merging it now would overstate the proof.
